steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Representation in UK film is shaped by the specific social, cultural and political dynamics of British society, where class, region, ethnicity and national identity intersect in distinctive ways.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Class representation is central to British cinema in ways that have no direct equivalent in Hollywood, with social realism making working-class experience a primary rather than marginal subject.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Regional identity representation challenges the London-centric bias of British media, giving voice to the cultures, dialects and experiences of Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland and England's regions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ethnic representation in UK film has evolved from near-invisibility through stereotyping towards greater complexity, though significant under-representation and typecasting persist.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Why is class representation more central to British cinema than to Hollywood? | Q: How does regional representation challenge dominant narratives of British identity? | Q: How has ethnic representation in UK film evolved and what issues remain?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Focus on specifically British aspects of representation — class, region, national identity — rather than treating representation generically. Use precise class and regional terminology: accent, dialect, setting, cultural markers — show how film language constructs these identities. Compare how your film represents Britishness with other traditions — heritage versus social realism — to show what is distinctive. Consider how intersectional identities in your film complicate simple readings of representation. Link representation to the UK industry context: how do funding structures and cultural policy influence what gets represented?
